headline: Chris White, chief executive of BondCliQ, says bond investors are beginning to doubt the long-term prospects of some of the biggest AI spenders, citing CoreWeave and Oracle.
score_reason: Facts match the headline; it is one market commentator's view from a TV interview.
importance_line: Investors in AI company bonds and, if bond supply swamps the market, the US government's own borrowing costs are affected; the doubt is that this is one commentator's reading.
summary: Chris White, chief executive of BondCliQ and ViableMkts, told CNBC on 14 Oct 2026 that bond investors are starting to doubt the long-term prospects of many large AI 'hyperscalers', the biggest cloud and AI spenders, pointing to CoreWeave and Oracle. He said their debt matures soon, so they must refinance within five to seven years and may have to pay a yield premium, and that heavy bond supply from AI firms could also make it harder for the US government to raise money.
